lines.japanese: 金を出してまでってほどじゃないんだけど、ちょろっと夕刊が読みたくて、俺は始発ホームで折り返し発進を待っている急行列車の網棚を、端から端まで探して歩いたんだ。
lines.english: I didn’t want one badly enough to pay for it, but I did feel like skimming the evening paper. So I walked the length of an express waiting at the departure platform for its return run, searching every luggage rack from end to end.

lines.japanese: でもこんな日にかぎって、ぬるいエログラビアが売りのゴシップ週刊誌しか手に入らなかった。
lines.english: Naturally, the one day I tried, all I could find was a gossip weekly whose sole attraction was its halfhearted cheesecake spreads.

lines.japanese: 駅周辺のゴミ箱も最近はテロ対策だか何だかで、捨て口が小さくなっていたり、回収用の扉が施錠されていたり、透明の覗き窓が付いていたりする。
lines.english: Lately, thanks to counterterrorism or some such thing, the trash cans around the station had narrow slots, locked collection doors, and transparent inspection panels.

lines.japanese: 世知辛い時代になったもんだよな。
lines.english: What an unforgiving world we lived in.

lines.japanese: ──と、透けて見える新聞紙を恨めしげに眺めつつぼやいたら、横にいた非認可のリサイクル業を営む住所不定のおっちゃんが、シミだらけの顔を得意げにほころばせた。
lines.english: —I muttered that while glaring bitterly at a newspaper visible through the clear panel. Beside me, a gentleman of no fixed address engaged in the unlicensed recycling trade broke into a proud smile across his mottled face.

lines.japanese: やつは先端が鉤状になってる鉄の棒を狭いゴミ捨て口に突っこむと、新聞の折り目に引っかけてそいつを器用にサルベージした。
lines.english: He fed an iron rod with a hooked tip through the narrow slot, caught it in the newspaper's fold, and salvaged the thing with practiced skill.

lines.japanese: 芸能スポーツ中心のタブロイド紙じゃなくて、日本でいちばん読まれてるあの新聞だ。俺はおっちゃんの手際を誉めたたえてから、ゴシップ週刊誌と交換してもらった。
lines.english: And it wasn't some celebrity-and-sports tabloid. It was *that* paper, the most widely read in Japan. After praising the old man's technique to the skies, I got him to trade it for my gossip weekly.

lines.japanese: それからしばらくおっちゃんと話をした。もちろん初対面だけど、どうせ一期一会でお互い遠慮する必要がなかったせいか、わりと話は弾んだ。
lines.english: Then we talked for a while. We'd never met before, naturally, but perhaps because we never expected to meet again, neither of us had any reason to hold back. The conversation flowed surprisingly well.

lines.japanese: おっちゃんは半生を捧げたカメラ屋が倒産する数十年前、大学で哲学を専攻していたそうで、ゴミ箱にまつわるよしなしごとをやたらと感慨深く語った。
lines.english: The old man said that, decades before the camera shop to which he'd devoted half his life went bankrupt, he'd majored in philosophy at university. He discoursed with enormous feeling upon sundry matters pertaining to trash cans.

lines.japanese: たとえば雑誌ひとつ取っても、おっちゃんたちが拾いやすいようにわざわざゴミ箱の上へ平置きしていくやつもいれば、逆に拾われないよう表紙を破ってから投機するやつもいるって話。
lines.english: Take a single magazine. Some people went out of their way to lay it flat atop the bin so men like him could collect it easily. Others tore off the cover before throwing it away expressly to keep anyone from collecting it.

lines.japanese: たとえばおっちゃんたちがゴミの持ち出ししていくのを、ある程度見て見ぬふりしてくれる業者もいれば、親の仇のごとく厳しく取りしまる役人もいるって話。
lines.english: Some businesses were willing, within reason, to pretend they hadn't seen his colleagues carry off the trash. Some officials cracked down as though the men had murdered their parents.

lines.japanese: 街には多様な恣意や故意が溢れ、それが一方では誰かを助け、また一方ではべつの誰かを困らせたりしている。なべて世は今日もそうして回るのだよ青年、とかって話。
lines.english: The city overflows with whims and intentions of every kind; here they help someone, there they trouble someone else. And thus, young man, the world continues to turn today. That sort of thing.

lines.japanese: 舌がノッたおっちゃんは、さらに言語の構造がもたらす人間性・社会性について一席ぶち始めたが、合間にエロ週刊誌をぱらぱらめくると、あるヌードモデルの奔放過ぎる陰毛について率直な不満を並べはじめた。
lines.english: Now thoroughly warmed to his theme, the old man launched into a lecture on human nature and social behavior produced by the structure of language. Then, leafing through the dirty weekly between observations, he began candidly listing his objections to one nude model’s excessively free-spirited pubic hair.

lines.japanese: 俺はそれを聞きながしながら、手に入れたばかりの夕刊をその場で広げた。三面記事と地方版にざっと目を通す。柳木原の小さな戦争は一行たりとも世間に知れわたっていなかった。
lines.english: I let that wash past me and opened my newly acquired evening paper on the spot. I skimmed the crime pages and the local section. Not one line about Yanagihara's little war had reached the world at large.

lines.japanese: 俺はおっちゃんに新聞を返して駅をあとにした。キャッチ＆リリース。なべて世は今日もこうして回っておるのだよ。よく分かんねーけど。
lines.english: I returned the paper to the old man and left the station. Catch and release. And thus did the world continue to turn today. Not that I really understood.
